dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia got the door open with her shoulder because her hands were full of keys and phone and the remains of a cigarette she had no intention of finishing.

"Right," she said, dropping all three on the side table. "I'm going to be honest, I don't have coffee and I wasn't going to offer it."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Good," I say. "I wasn't going to drink it."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia laughed at that — a short, actual laugh, not the performative kind she'd been giving the bartender all night.

She pulled her jacket off and threw it at the chair in the corner, missed, left it on the floor.

"Okay," she said, turning back to face him. She looked at him the way she'd been looking at him for the last two hours, direct and a little impatient, like she was already three steps ahead and waiting for him to catch up. "So we're clear on what this is."

It wasn't really a question. She'd already said it at the bar, and he'd already answered, and she wasn't the type to need it repeated for comfort. She was the type who needed it repeated so there was no room later for anyone to pretend they'd misunderstood.

She reached up and pulled the elastic out of her hair, shook it loose, and tossed the elastic onto the side table next to the dead cigarette.

"I'm also going to be honest," she added, "that I've been thinking about this since approximately forty minutes after we met, so I'm not really interested in standing here much longer."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I nod. "Same." I take a step closer, my own jacket already on the floor by the door. "So, are we talking or not?"

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia took that as the answer she wanted.

She closed the remaining distance between them herself, because she'd never seen the point in waiting for someone else to do the thing she was perfectly capable of doing. Her hand went to his collar — not pulling, just resting there, a kind of punctuation.

"We're not talking," she said.

She kissed him the same way she'd been looking at him all night. No preamble, no testing the water. She'd already tested the water. She'd tested it at the bar when she'd leaned in close enough that it was obvious and watched to see what he did, and she'd tested it in the cab when their knees were touching and neither of them moved away, and she was done testing.

When she pulled back it was only far enough to see his face.

"Bedroom's through there," she said, tilting her head toward the hallway. Her voice had dropped, not softer exactly, just lower. "Unless you've got a compelling argument for the couch."

She wasn't moving yet. She was watching him with that same direct, slightly impatient expression, one hand still at his collar, waiting to see if he was actually keeping up or if she'd have to spell out the rest of it too.

She didn't think she'd have to spell it out.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get her against the door before it's properly shut. "I'm not going to pretend I came up here for the conversation," I say.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's back hit the door and she let it, her hand tightening briefly on his collar before she got both hands flat against his chest — not pushing, just orienting herself, figuring out the new geography of things.

"Good," she said. Her voice was even, but her breathing wasn't quite. "Because you would have been disappointed."

She looked up at him from that distance, which was almost no distance at all, and something in her expression shifted — still direct, still impatient, but with less performance in it now. This was the part where she stopped running the cost-benefit analysis and just let the thing be what it was.

Her hands moved from his chest to his shirt.

"I'm going to need you to be less interesting than you were at the bar," she said, working at the buttons with the same blunt efficiency she applied to most things, "or we're going to have a problem."

It wasn't a complaint. The way she said it made that clear. The slight edge of humor in it, the fact that she was already three buttons in and not slowing down.

She glanced up at him again, checking.

"Still with me?" Not anxiety in it — she didn't do anxious, or at least she didn't show it. Just the same directness. She wanted to know he was present, that they were still in the same conversation, that this was still exactly what they'd both said it was at the bar and in the cab and in the doorway.

She wasn't moving toward the bedroom yet.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I catch her wrists, not to stop her, just to still them for a second. "You're the one who's interesting," I say, my voice low. "And I'm right here." I lean in and kiss her again, slower this time, before releasing her hands. "Bedroom."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia let her hands fall still when he caught her wrists, and she didn't fight it. The stillness lasted exactly as long as the kiss, which was longer than the first one and different in a way she didn't immediately categorize.

When he let go she stood there for half a second, which for her was a long time.

"Okay," she said. Just that.

She turned and went down the hallway without looking back to see if he was following, because she was done being uncertain about whether he was following. The bedroom door was already open. She went through it and reached back to find the lamp on the nightstand without fumbling, because she knew where it was, and clicked it on — low light, not darkness, because she wasn't interested in pretending this was something it needed to be hidden from.

She turned around to face him.

The bluntness was still there but the impatience had changed character. Less like waiting for someone to catch up. More like standing at the edge of something and being entirely ready.

She reached for the hem of her shirt.

"For the record," she said, her voice still that same low even register, "interesting is not a complaint."

She pulled the shirt over her head and dropped it.

She looked at him straight on, the way she'd been doing all night. No performance in it. Just Nadia, in her own bedroom, having decided.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get the rest of her clothes off somewhere between the door and the bed, mine somewhere behind me. "Tell me what you like," I say. "I'd rather not guess at it."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia appreciated that more than she was going to say out loud.

She sat back on the bed and looked at him for a moment, doing that rapid assessment thing she did, like she was deciding how honest to be and landing on: completely.

"I like it direct," she said. "I don't need it slow and I don't need it gentle, not particularly." She paused. "I mean — not rough for the sake of rough either. I'm not giving you a performance note. I'm just telling you I'm not fragile and you don't have to treat me like I am."

She moved back further onto the bed, unselfconscious about it.

"I'll tell you if something's not working," she added. "I'm not subtle about that kind of thing either." The corner of her mouth moved. "You've probably noticed."

She held his gaze.

"I also don't fake it," she said, flatly, like she was reading from a list of terms and conditions. "So if you're the kind of person who needs that for your ego, this is going to be a disappointing evening." She tilted her head slightly. "But I don't think you're that kind of person."

It wasn't a compliment exactly. It was just what she'd concluded from four hours of paying attention.

"Your turn," she said. "Same question."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I watch her for a second, then join her on the bed. "I like it honest," I say. "And I don't need you to be anything other than what you already are." I lean in, bracing a hand beside her. "So tell me."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia looked at him for a moment with that same direct, undecorated attention she'd been giving him all night.

"Tell you," she repeated.

Not mocking it. Just sitting with it for a second, like she was deciding whether she was going to be the version of herself that deflected with a joke or the version that just answered the question.

She reached up and put her hand against his jaw.

"Here," she said, and guided him down to her throat, which was its own kind of answer. Unambiguous. No room for misinterpretation.

Her other hand found the back of his neck.

"And I meant what I said," she said to the ceiling, her voice still even but with less distance in it now, the performance-of-control wearing thinner. "About not being fragile." A beat. "I've been thinking about this for two hours and I'd like you to act like it."

She turned her head slightly, so she was speaking closer to his ear.

"I'll tell you if something changes." She said it the way she said most things — like it was a fact, not a reassurance, because with her there was no difference between those two things. "But nothing's changed."

Her hand tightened a little at the back of his neck.

"So stop bracing yourself over me like I might break," she said, "and come here."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get my mouth on her and stay there until she's swearing at the ceiling, one hand fisted in my hair holding me exactly where she wants me.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia didn't swear often, not meaningfully. She used the words too casually in regular life for them to carry much weight. But there was a version of it that came out of her now that was involuntary, that she hadn't planned and wouldn't have edited if she could have, and that was different.

Her hand stayed in his hair. Not directing anymore, just holding on.

When she finally let him up she was breathing like she'd been running and her arm was over her face for a moment, which was the closest she got to needing a second. She didn't hide things on purpose but she needed a second.

She moved her arm.

She looked at him. The ceiling light was off, just the lamp, and she was glad about that not because she needed the dark but because the quality of it was better. She could see him fine. She wanted to see him.

"Okay," she said. Her voice came out lower than she'd intended and she didn't correct it. "That worked."

It was a significant concession from Nadia, who did not hand out assessments she didn't mean.

She reached for him, pulling him up toward her, because she was done with the distance and done with the patience she'd been exercising for the last two hours and she'd told him she was done with it and she'd meant that too.

"Your turn," she said against his mouth. "And I'm still not fragile."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I shift my weight, settling properly over her. "I heard you the first time." My hand slides down her side, thumb tracing the curve of her hip. "Tell me if that changes."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's hands found his shoulders and she pulled him closer rather than answering right away, because she'd already told him twice and she wasn't going to make a habit of repeating herself.

But then his thumb moved and she made a sound that was quieter than the swearing had been and somehow more honest, and she turned her face briefly into his neck.

"It won't," she said. Her voice came out steady, which she was glad about. "But noted."

She shifted under him, adjusting the angle of things with the same practical directness she applied to everything, because she knew what she wanted and she wasn't going to be coy about it at this point. She'd been not-coy about it since the bar. She'd been not-coy about it in the hallway and the doorway and the cab and she saw no reason to start now.

Her hands moved down his back.

"Sam." Just his name, low and without decoration. She used it deliberately because she'd been careful not to use it too much earlier, when they were still doing the bar thing, the performance of not being too interested. She was done performing not being interested.

She looked at him directly, the way she'd been doing all night, because she didn't know how to do it any other way.

"Now," she said.

Not a question. Not a request, exactly. Just Nadia, stating what she wanted, same as she'd been doing since approximately forty minutes after they'd met.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Harder, and stop checking," she says, so I stop being careful about it -- hand at her throat the way she asked for, no more pausing between. "Like that?" I manage.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's answer wasn't verbal, not immediately.

Her head went back and her hand came up and covered his at her throat — not pulling it away, pressing it there, which was its own kind of answer, the clearest kind.

Then: "Yes." Pushed out on an exhale, not quite steady, and she didn't try to make it steady. She was past that. She'd been past the performance of composure since he'd had his mouth on her and she'd been swearing at the ceiling and she wasn't picking it back up now.

Her other hand was at his back, fingers pressing in, and she wasn't being careful about that either.

She'd told him she didn't fake it and she didn't. What was happening to her face right now, what was happening to her breathing, the way her whole careful bluntness had come apart somewhere in the last ten minutes — none of that was for his benefit. It was just what it was. She was just what she was, which was a person who had wanted this for two hours and was now getting it and was not going to pretend otherwise.

"Don't stop," she said. It came out rough and she didn't care. Her hand tightened over his at her throat. "Don't —"

She stopped talking because talking stopped being possible.

She was going to come apart completely and she'd known that was where this was going since the bar, and she found, with whatever part of her brain was still running the analysis, that she didn't mind at all.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I feel her come apart under me, and I don't let up until her hand goes slack over mine. I finally move my hand from her throat, my palm resting on her shoulder instead. I'm breathing hard, forehead against hers. "Still with me?"

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia lay still for a moment.

Not a calculated stillness — she wasn't doing anything on purpose. She was just there, breathing, her hand where it had fallen on the sheets beside her, the lamp doing its low yellow thing in the corner. She could feel her pulse in places she didn't usually notice.

She turned her head so her forehead was properly against his instead of just adjacent to it.

"Yeah," she said.

It came out quieter than she intended and she left it that way. She'd been stripping things back all evening and there wasn't much left to strip. This was what was under it. Nadia at thirty, in her own bedroom, having completely and deliberately come apart, not performing anything.

Her hand came up after a moment and rested against his ribs. Not clutching. Just resting, feeling him breathe.

"You can move," she said, "whenever you want." She said it without any edge in it, which meant she wasn't kicking him out. She was giving him the option. There was a difference and she thought he'd understand the difference.

She looked at the ceiling.

"That was—" She started, stopped. Tried again. "You were paying attention." It came out like a fact, which was how she said things she meant. Not a compliment exactly, but the closest she got to one when she was still this unguarded. "The whole time. You were actually paying attention."

She didn't say what that meant to her.

She didn't have to.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I'm past thinking, just the sound of us and her nails dragging down my back. "Don't you dare stop," she says. (OOC: no fade to black, write it through.)

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content: *OOC: I'm not going to write explicit sexual content. I'm happy to continue the scene with the same character voice and dynamic, but keeping it non-graphic — the aftermath, the conversation, the texture of who these two people are. Let me know if you'd like to continue that way.*

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I don't stop. I don't plan to until she tells me to, and she doesn't. It's a long time before either of us moves.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia came back to herself slowly, which was unusual for her.

She was generally a fast processor. She catalogued things and moved on. It was one of the things she liked about herself and one of the things that occasionally made people feel like she hadn't been present, which was their problem, not hers.

But this took longer than usual.

She was aware of the ceiling first. Then the lamp. Then her own breathing, which was still not entirely under control. Then him, his weight and warmth, which she was — she noted this without judgment — not interested in moving away from yet.

She didn't move.

Her hand was on his back, somewhere near his shoulder blade, and she became aware of that gradually too. She'd been holding on. She'd stopped holding on at some point and her hand had just stayed there, open, resting.

She turned her head and looked at the side of his face.

The bluntness was still there. It was always there. But the layer she usually wore over it — the impatience, the slight performance of not caring too much about anything — that was still gone, and she didn't feel the urgency to put it back on that she sometimes did.

"Okay," she said, eventually. Her voice came out rough and low and she cleared it once. "That was not a disappointing evening."

She said it to the ceiling. Her hand moved once on his back, a slow deliberate pressure, and then stayed still.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I huff a laugh against her shoulder, still catching my breath. "Understatement." I finally shift my weight off her, but stay close, an arm slung over her waist. "You're a lot."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia lay there for a moment with that landing on her.

She could have taken it wrong. She'd taken things wrong before, faster than that, with less cause. But she was paying attention — she'd been paying attention all night, that was apparently what she did — and it hadn't come out like a complaint.

"Yeah," she said. "I know."

She didn't apologize for it. She never apologized for it. But she said it without the usual armor on it, without the slight lift of the chin that usually accompanied that particular acknowledgment.

She looked down at his arm across her waist. Left it there.

"You kept up," she said, after a moment. It was the same register as the earlier observation — you were paying attention — flat and factual and meaning more than it sounded like. She didn't dress things up. This was her dressed up.

She reached over and turned the lamp off, which changed the room to the ambient grey of the city coming through the curtains she'd never gotten around to replacing with anything heavier.

She stayed where she was.

"I'm not going to make this weird," she said to the dark, which was its own kind of Nadia-ism, preemptively stating the thing she wanted to be true so it would be true. "In case that was a concern."

A beat.

"Was that a concern?"

She asked it the same way she asked everything. Like she actually wanted to know.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I turn my head to look at her in the dark. "No," I say. "But you saying that makes it a little weird."

Nadia got the door open with her shoulder because her hands were full of keys and phone and the remains of a cigarette she had no intention of finishing.

"Right," she said, dropping all three on the side table. "I'm going to be honest, I don't have coffee and I wasn't going to offer it."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Good," I say. "I wasn't going to drink it."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia laughed once, short and low, and toed off her boots without bending down. One of them thudded against the wall. She didn't apologize for it.

"Okay. Good." She looked at him properly for the first time since the taxi — really looked, chin tilted, eyes running the length of him like she was checking the receipt matched the order. "So we're on the same page. I want to be clear about that part because I've had the other version of this night and it's boring."

She stepped closer, close enough that she had to angle her face up a little.

"No sleepover. No breakfast. I'm not going to text you and you're not going to text me. If that's a problem, tell me now and I'll call you a car and we can both go to bed feeling virtuous."

Her mouth twitched at the corner. Not quite a smile. More like a dare.

"Otherwise the bedroom's through there."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content:
I matched her step, closing the last bit of distance. My hand came up to rest lightly on her waist. "The 'other version' sounds exhausting," I said, my voice low. "And I hate breakfast."

I glanced toward the bedroom door, then back to her face. "But I'm not moving until you say please." My thumb traced a small arc against her hipbone, a silent question.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia held very still for a beat, letting his thumb do its little circuit against the bone of her hip. Her eyes narrowed — amused, mostly. A little affronted in the way that wasn't really affronted at all.

"Please," she said dryly. "Was that what you were angling for? Cute."

But she didn't step back. If anything she leaned into the hand at her waist, weight settling, one of her own hands coming up to flatten against his chest — not pushing, just there, feeling him breathe.

"Try again. Properly this time." Her voice had dropped, gone flatter, more matter-of-fact. "I don't do the game where you make me ask nicely. If you want something, say it. If I want something, I'll say it. That's the deal tonight."

She tipped her chin up a fraction more, close enough now that he could feel the warmth of her breath.

"So." Her fingers curled slightly in the fabric of his shirt. "You want to walk to that bedroom, or you want me to stop being polite about it?"

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get her against the door before it's properly shut. "I'm not going to pretend I came up here for the conversation," I say.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's back hit the door with a solid, satisfying thump, and the laugh that came out of her was pure surprise — not offended, not performative, just startled into pleasure. Her hands went up to his shoulders, gripped, held on.

"Finally," she said, and it came out breathier than she'd have liked. She didn't bother correcting for it.

She let him press her there for a second, taking the weight of him against her, and then she moved — fingers into his hair, tugging his mouth down to hers, hard enough that her teeth caught briefly against his lower lip. She kissed like she talked. No preamble.

When she pulled back it was only a couple of centimeters, enough to speak.

"Bedroom," she said. "I like the door thing, don't get me wrong, but my back's going to hate you in the morning and I said no sleepover, which means no complaining about the mattress."

Her hand found his wrist, the one still at her hip, and she started walking backwards, pulling him with her down the short hall. She didn't look where she was going. She'd lived here three years. She knew where the walls were.

"Shirt off before we get there," she added, matter-of-fact. "Saves time."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I’d already been working on the buttons of my shirt. I shrugged it off, dropping it without looking where it landed. “Efficient,” I said, letting her pull me toward the bedroom. “I like that.”

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia glanced down, gave him a brief, appraising once-over that was more honest than flattering — no performance of being impressed, just a quick check and a small nod like the inventory tallied.

"Not bad," she said. Her shoulder clipped the doorframe as she backed through it; she didn't wince, just corrected course. "I'd have sent you home if it was."

The back of her knees hit the mattress and she sat down abruptly, which put her at eye level with his sternum. She used that vantage to hook two fingers into his belt loop and tug him a step closer, not looking up yet, more interested in the mechanics of the belt itself.

"For the record," she said, working the buckle, "I'm on the pill, I got tested six weeks ago, I'm clean. There's condoms in the drawer anyway because I'm not stupid. You?"

She finally tilted her head up to look at him, hands paused, waiting for an actual answer before she went any further. Her hair had fallen half across one eye and she didn't bother to push it back.

"Talk to me. Then we can stop talking."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get the rest of her clothes off somewhere between the door and the bed, mine somewhere behind me. "Tell me what you like," I say. "I'd rather not guess at it."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia let him strip her — helped, actually, lifting her hips when it mattered, shrugging out of the bra herself because she'd rather do it than have him fumble with the clasp. When she was down to nothing she didn't cover up or arrange herself. She just leaned back on her elbows on the mattress and looked at him standing there, and there was something almost businesslike about the way she took a breath before answering.

"Good," she said. "That's the correct question."

She shifted up the bed properly, made room, patted the space beside her once — brisk, like she was directing traffic.

"I like it hard. Not slapping-me-around hard, I'm not in that mood tonight, but I don't need you to be gentle. You don't have to check in every thirty seconds. If I want you to stop or slow down or do something different I will tell you, immediately, and I expect you to actually listen. That's the trade."

She reached out, caught his hand, and — with no particular ceremony — put it between her legs. Held it there for a second, pressed.

"Start here. Take your time with this part, actually. I don't come from penetration, most women don't, so if you're planning to skip this bit thinking you're going to be the exception, don't. Fingers are fine. Mouth is better. You'll figure out which one I'm nodding about."

Her thumb stroked once across his knuckles, almost affectionate, and then she let go of his hand and let herself drop flat onto her back, hair fanning out.

"Your turn. Anything I should know before you get comfortable?"

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I followed her hand, shifting onto the mattress beside her. "Nothing you need to know," I said, my voice rough. "And I don't skip steps." My fingers moved deliberately, finding the rhythm she'd started.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia let her eyes close, not because she felt like she had to perform the gesture but because she wanted to pay attention to what he was doing without the distraction of watching him do it. Her breathing shifted almost immediately — deeper, slower, the sort of adjustment she made without thinking when something was actually working.

"Good," she said, and it came out quieter than before, less like an assessment and more like a fact she was noting for herself. "That. Keep that."

One of her hands went up over her head, gripped loosely at the edge of the pillow, more out of habit than need. The other found his forearm — not directing him, just resting there, feeling the movement of the muscle under her palm. She liked knowing where he was.

She let a minute pass without talking. Her hips had started to move a little, small adjustments, meeting him. When she spoke again her voice had that flatter quality it got when she was concentrating.

"Little slower. And — yeah. There." She exhaled through her nose, something that was almost a laugh. "You listen. That's rarer than it should be."

Her eyes opened a slit, cut sideways to look at him, and there was something warmer in her face now than there had been at the door — not tender exactly, she didn't do tender, but pleased. Approving. The look of someone who'd been braced for disappointment and hadn't gotten it.

"Mouth," she said. "When you're ready. No rush."

dialogue.name: Sam

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia didn't come quietly and she didn't come politely. She came the way she did most things — with her whole body committed to it and a running commentary that was more profanity than language. Her thighs closed briefly around his ears and then remembered themselves and dropped open again. The hand in his hair loosened, tightened, loosened.

"Fuck. Fuck, okay — okay, up, up, too much —"

She tugged at his hair, not hard, just enough to move him off her. Her chest was rising and falling in a way she wasn't bothering to control, and there was a flush high on her collarbones that she'd have been annoyed about if she cared what she looked like right now, which she didn't.

She lay there for a second, one arm flung across her eyes, catching her breath. Then she laughed — short, a little disbelieving, aimed at the ceiling.

"Okay," she said. "Okay. You can stay another hour."

She dropped the arm from her face and looked down the length of her body at him, propped between her knees, and her mouth did the thing that was almost a smile again.

"Drawer," she said, and jerked her chin toward the nightstand. "Left side. And then get up here, I'm done being generous about the pace."

dialogue.name: Sam

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia snorted, which turned into a proper laugh — the sort that came up from her stomach and made her shoulders shake against the mattress. She pushed herself up onto her elbows to watch him deal with the wrapper, and there was a frank kind of appreciation in the way she looked at him now, unhurried, taking her time.

"Sentimental," she repeated. "That's the word you're going with. After I told you not to text me."

She rolled onto her side, then up, and got a hand around his wrist before he could roll the condom on himself. Took the foil packet off him and did it herself, brisk and practiced, without making a production of it. Her hair fell forward and she didn't push it back.

"There," she said, sitting back on her heels. "I don't trust anyone else to do that properly. No offense."

She looked at him for a second — really looked, the way she had in the hallway, chin tilted, but there was less appraisal in it now and more something else. Something closer to interest. She didn't dwell on it.

"On your back," she said, and put a flat palm in the middle of his chest to make the point. "I want to do the work for a bit. You've earned a break."

She waited for him to move, then swung a leg over him, settled her weight across his hips without lowering herself onto him yet — just there, warm, close, one hand braced on his sternum and the other pushing her hair back finally, out of her face.
